subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum & subprocessors — DPA redlines
messages:
From: Julie Black <julie.black@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@outsidecounsel.com>
Date: 2025-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: CCPA/CPRA addendum: redlines and subprocessors

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are Acme Health's standard DPA redlines — the primary points for us are: 1) explicit "service provider / processor" language for CPRA (avoid any "sale" or joint-controller constructs), 2) a clear subprocessors notice and approval process (we usually require 30 days' notice and registration), and 3) a US-only processing option for health data.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is prepared to:
- Accept CPRA service-provider-only obligations (no sale, limited use for advertising profiling),
- Provide a rolling subprocessor registry and at least 30 days prior notice for new subprocessors (with an expedited process for critical security patches), and
- Agree to a contractual limitation on cross-border transfers for Acme data unless Acme expressly instructs otherwise?

We also looped in our outside counsel, John Smith, on the redlines. Please review and let us know if Redwood can sign the DPA with these addenda or propose targeted language.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redlines.pdf

Thanks,
Julie Black
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum: redlines and subprocessors

Julie — thanks for the note and the redlines. Looping Neha (internal legal) and Laura (Sales Ops) so we can coordinate the response. I read your three asks and wanted to confirm Redwood's starting position:

- Service provider / processor language: yes — Redwood's DPA is drafted on a processor/service-provider basis (we do not treat customer data as a sale). I can push our latest DPA draft for your review (attached: redwood_dpa_v3_summary.pdf).
- Subprocessors: we maintain a public registry and typically provide 30 days' notice for planned additions. For critical security patches or emergency replacements we notify as soon as possible and describe mitigations.
- US-only processing option: we can accommodate routing/processing constraints by customer contract but need to confirm operational limits for certain hosted services. Neha — can you confirm the precise language we should offer for a US-only clause and any required operational caveats?

Next steps: Neha will propose CPRA addendum wording; if Acme is comfortable we can push a DocuSign request and include the subprocessor inventory. Laura — I may need a short SOW or MSA pointer for the US-only hosting cost delta.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Proposed CPRA addendum language and subprocessor procedure

Hi Julie & Karthik,

Thanks — I reviewed Acme's redlines and Karthik's summary. Below is a proposed reply that we can track as redlines in the DPA. I pasted it into the thread for visibility; happy to convert to tracked changes in redwood_dpa_v3.docx if that helps.

Key points Redwood can accept (proposed contractual wording):
1) Service provider (CPRA) commitment: "Redwood will act only as a Service Provider/Processor with respect to Customer Personal Information and will not retain, use, or disclose such Personal Information for any purpose other than for the specific, limited purposes set forth in the Agreement or as required by law."

2) Subprocessors: "Redwood will maintain an up-to-date subprocessor registry at [link] and will provide at least thirty (30) days' prior notice via email to the Customer before engaging any new subprocessor. For engagements required to remediate a critical security incident, Redwood will provide notice as soon as practicable and document compensating controls; Customer will have the right to object within ten (10) calendar days. If Customer objects, parties will meet in good faith to agree on risk mitigation or replacement; if no agreement, Customer may suspend processing for the impacted data types until a solution is implemented."

3) US-only processing: "Customer may instruct Redwood to restrict processing of Customer Personal Information to data centers located within the United States. Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to comply and will document any residual routing or third-party processing that may require cross-border transfer. Any operational constraints or cost delta will be documented in an addendum to the SOW."

4) CPRA-specific protections: explicit "no sale" statement, limited profiling uses, and cooperation with consumer rights requests (right to know, access, deletion, correction). Redwood will support reasonable data export formats and provide an API for bulk export of consumer data upon request per the Agreement.

Attachments we can provide now: redwood_dpa_v3.docx (tracked changes version), subprocessors_inventory.csv (current registry), redwood_dpa_v3_summary.pdf (summary of key clauses). Also we can share SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA or secure portal.

DocuSign: if Acme is broadly aligned, I can send a DocuSign envelope with the DPA + CPRA addendum + an SOW note for US-only hosting. Link: https://docusign.com/req/abc123

Please advise on any non-starters. If Acme needs stricter notice periods or an unconditional right to approve new subprocessors, flag the specific subprocessors so we can consider carve-outs.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3.docx; subprocessors_inventory.csv; redwood_dpa_v3_summary.pdf

Subject: Re: Proposed CPRA addendum language and subprocessor procedure

Neha — thank you for the detailed draft language. A few quick items from our side after internal review and counsel feedback:

- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable. We would like one small edit to the objection period: extend to fifteen (15) calendar days for larger data classes (PHI/health data) so we have adequate time to validate risk.
- US-only processing: Acme requires a contractual guarantee that health-related personal data for California residents be processed in the US; that can be a carve-out in the SOW. Please confirm Redwood will accept that carve-out for PHI scoped to Acme datasets.
- Audits/SOC2: we will need SOC 2 Type II and an option for a vendor security questionnaire. Can Redwood provide the SOC report via secure share? We can execute an NDA if required.

If the minor edits above are acceptable, we are happy to proceed to signature. We will also attach a short "processing requirements" doc with sample data classes so you can confirm the operational feasibility.

Attachments: Acme_processing_requirements.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to final language.

Best,
Julie Black
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health
